summary: Superpowers reports eval results in its design specs and release notes: subagent-driven-development cost runs show -32% time, -37% tokens and -27% dollars on go-fractals and -21% / -28% / -25% on svelte-todo versus baseline, with typical mid-band savings of ~20-25% across 8 go-fractals runs. These cost runs and the hand-scored pressure tests (5 reps per arm) are written up as results in the specs, while their harness is in the separate superpowers-evals repo; release-note figures such as "roughly twice as fast" and "almost 50% fewer tokens" are stated without data. The worktree-preference test is an in-repo harness whose result (50/50 runs) is stated in a comment in the script, with no committed output. The docs also report results that did not favor the changes: all 25 baseline reps already refused to treat a ledger as license to skip work, so the hypothesized failure did not reproduce, and the resume tool-call count did not drop (9.6 vs 9.0).
